note: 'the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord' (Rom 6:23), which puts both figures in one verse and the atonement between them. 1 Corinthians 15:3 is the formula: 'Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures'.
Birth and life, in the chapter that also gives everlasting life at 3:16.
'Baptized into his death ... buried with Him through baptism into death' (Rom 6:3-4).
'we too may walk in newness of life' (Rom 6:4).
'I have been crucified with Christ' (Gal 2:20), and 'you died' (Col 3:3) -- **said of the living**, which is the sense of death this figure carries.

The figure, back to the place. 'Carrying His own cross, He went out to The Place of the Skull' (John 19:17). **The word carries the event with it wherever Paul uses it**, which is why the two are joined here and not merged.
'he must deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me' (Luke 9:23), and the same at Matthew 16:24.
'through whom we have now received reconciliation' (Rom 5:11).
'Or aren't you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?' (Rom 6:3).

'I have been crucified with Christ' (Gal 2:20), and 'our old self was crucified with Him' (Rom 6:6).; 'I have been crucified with Christ' (Gal 2:20), and 'the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world' (Gal 6:14). **Twice, in one letter, with the direction reversed the second time.**
